title: Why Are You Cast Down, O My Soul?
summary: David doesn't let his heart stay cold. He remembers. Recall God's mercies, and command your soul to hope in God.
exhortation: My call to you this morning is to remember all his great mercies toward you. Look at what David does. He doesn't let his heart stay cold toward the Lord. He starts recounting the joy of being with God's people.

Do you remember that? Think of the last time you were at church and your heart was so full you couldn't wait for the first song, when you'd be the first one through the door, like David leading the procession to the house of God. Maybe you walked in and saw that precious saint who's battling cancer, with a huge smile, ready to worship Jesus. They had more cause than most to be downcast, but their lips were praising God, and it inspired you. Being with God's people spurs us to worship.
Recall the moment you were saved. Remember when you knew that the blood of Jesus was shed for you, not just as an idea, but for you, and the hope that filled your heart.

So command your soul this morning: "Soul, praise the Lord. Hope in God. I will again praise him." I won't be satisfied with a soul that is cold and in turmoil. Lord Jesus, I want you to be my delight and my salvation this morning.
prayer: Lord, I pray for every person waking up this morning with a heavy heart, perhaps dreading the day, fearful or full of anxiety. By your Spirit, comfort them and fill them with faith and irrepressible joy: a joy that doesn't depend on the day's circumstances, but looks to you in faith, knowing you are with us and have paid for every sin.

Our greatest problem has been solved by you, Jesus, at the cross and when you rose from the grave. Let that define our day today, not our problems and anxieties, but your grace and the joy we have in you.
